A value below $F0 is a pattern number n and gives $F0/$F1 the byte at $B9E4+n, which the code reads twice, once into each of $F0 and $F1; if the repeat count is zero the track index advances, otherwise the count goes down and the index advances when it reaches zero. A value of $F0 or more is a track command, dispatched through $B89A and $B8A0 by the JMP operand at $B383.
Low byte of the address operand of the JMP at $B382, overwritten each time with the address of the track command handler to run.
High byte of the address operand of the JMP at $B382, overwritten each time with the address of the track command handler to run.
Track command $F0: sets the track index $B014,X to the next byte of the list and goes on reading the list at $B34E.
Track command $F1: stores the next byte in the repeat count $B06A,X, moves the track index $B014,X on by 2 and goes on at $B34E.
Track command $F2: stops the voice: clears its active flag $F7+X and the voice's registers $D404-$D406 and returns.
Track command $F3: stores the next byte in the transposition $B08D,X, moves the track index on by 2 and goes on at $B34E.
Track command $F4: stores the next byte in $B0BE, $B0BF and $B0C0, which starts a fade-out with that rate, moves the track index on by 2 and goes on at $B34E.

Track command $F5: stores the next byte in $B0C2, $B0BF and $B0C0, which starts a fade-in with that rate, sets $B0C1 and $D418 to $10, stores the byte after it in $B0C3 as the target volume, moves the track index on by 3 and goes on at $B34E.

Runs the current voice's wave program, called by $B176 for each active voice that is not playing a drum. Counts $B00A,X down and returns unless it reaches zero. At zero, if the pitch offset $B08A is set, it clears it and looks the frequency up again from the note $B067 plus the transposition $B08D in the tables $B8C2 and $B920. It then loads the program pointer $B020/$B026 into $F0/$F1, reads the command number at the position $B06D (starting at 0), stores the handler from $B8A6 and $B8AD in the JMP operand at $B440 and jumps to it. $B42B is where commands 1 and 2 read the next command.
Low byte of the address operand of the JMP at $B43F, overwritten each time with the address of the wave-program command handler to run.
High byte of the address operand of the JMP at $B43F, overwritten each time with the address of the wave-program command handler to run.
Wave-program command 0: stores the next byte as the number of frames to wait in $B00A,X and ends the step through $B4ED.
Wave-program command 1: loads $F0/$F1 with the two bytes that follow, a new program address, sets the position $B06D to 0 and carries on at $B42B in the same frame.
Wave-program command 2: stores the next two bytes in $B06F,X (attack/decay) and $B072,X (sustain/release), writes them to the voice's $D405 and $D406 and carries on at $B42B.
Wave-program command 3: writes the next byte to the voice's control register $D404 (waveform and gate) and stores the byte after it as the frames to wait in $B00A,X; ends the step through $B4ED.

Wave-program command 4: writes the next byte to the voice's $D404 like command 3, but the wait is the note's remaining count $B004,X minus the byte after it, so the step comes that many frames before the note ends.

Wave-program command 5: writes the next byte to the voice's $D404, stores the one after it as the frames to wait in $B00A,X and the third in $B084,X and $B08A,X, which asks for the frequency to be looked up again with that offset. When the third byte is 0 it instead sets the voice's frequency $B061/$B064 to $FFFF, clears $B084 and sets the offset to 1.

End of a wave-program step: adds 1 to the position $B06D and stores $F0/$F1 plus the position as the voice's wave pointer $B020/$B026. Wave-program command 6 enters here directly, so it skips one byte.

Stream command $81: the next byte n selects a wave program. The address at offset 2n of the table $BA7C is stored as the voice's program start $B023/$B029, which the next note copies to $B020/$B026. Carries on at $B25C.
Stream command $82: the three bytes that follow go to $B02F (start index into the table $B9E4), $B099 (initial pulse width, high byte) and $B093 (low byte). Carries on at $B25C.
Stream command $83: the next byte goes to $B038, the start index into the slide table $BA07. Sets the slide flag $B075 and clears $B032 and the arpeggio flag $B07B. Carries on at $B25C.

Stream commands $84 and $8D: clears the slide flag $B075 and sets the arpeggio flag $B07B. The next byte n selects the entry whose address is at offset 2n of the table $BA5B (kept in $F4/$F5); its first byte goes to $B0AE (frames per step), its second to $B0B4 (number of steps) and the address after them to $B03B/$B041. Carries on at $B25C.
Stream command $87: the next byte is stored in $B007,X and in the flag $B087,X, so that following notes carry no length byte. Carries on at $B25C.
Stream command $88: clears the fixed-length flag $B087,X so that notes carry a length byte again. Carries on at $B25C.

Stream commands $86 and $89: the next byte is an offset into the 5-byte records of the table $B97E. A record holds a list address, a list length (to $B0B8), a sustain/release value (to $D406 and $B081) and a pulse width high byte (to $D403). The list address goes to $B04F/$B055 and the address plus the length to $B052/$B058. It then writes 0 to $D405 and 8 to $D404, clears $B0BB, takes the byte after the offset as the note length $B004,X and returns without reading on; $B7B6 plays the list. It also restarts the filter sweep, copying $B047 to $B048, $B04B to $B04D and $B04C to $B04E and setting $B013 to 1.

Stream command $85: the first byte goes to $B047 (start index into the table $BA62), the second to $B04B and $B04D, the third to $B04C and $B04E, the fourth to the filter control register $D417 and to $B07E,X, after all three of $B07E are cleared. Carries on at $B25C.

Pulse-width sweep of the current voice. Counts $B00D,X down. At zero it reads a step from the table $B9E4 at the index $B02C,X: a frame count (to $B00D), a low and a high step (to $B09C and $B09F); a count of 0 means the next byte is a new index and the read is repeated. Every call it adds the step to the width $B090/$B096 and writes it to the voice's $D402 and $D403. Called by $B176.

Pitch slide of the current voice. Returns if $B075,X is zero. Counts $B010,X down. At zero it reads a step (frame count, low step, high step) from the table $BA07, or from $BA5B when $B032 is non-zero, at the index $B035,X into $B010, $B0A2 and $B0A5; a count of 0 means the next byte is a new index. Every call it adds the step to the frequency $B061/$B064. Called by $B176 before the frequency is written.

Arpeggio of the current voice. Returns if $B07B,X is zero. Counts $B0AB,X down; at zero it reloads it from $B0AE, reads the step at $B0B1,X from the list at $B03B/$B041, adds it to the note $B067 and the offsets $B08A and $B08D, looks the sum up in $B8C2 and $B920 and writes the frequency to the voice's $D400/$D401. $B0B1 is counted up and returns to 0 at $B0B4. Called by $B176.

Filter sweep, once per call. Counts $B013 down; at zero it reads a step from the table $BA62 at $B048: a frame count (to $B013), a low and a high step (to $B049 and $B04A); a count of 0 means the next byte is a new index. It adds the step to the 16-bit filter value (low byte $B04E, high byte $B04D) and writes the low three bits of its low byte to $D415 and bits 3 to 10 of the value to $D416. Called by $B176 after the voices.

Plays the drum lists of the three voices, X from 2 down to 0, for every voice with $B081 set. While the step count $B0BB differs from the list length $B0B8 it patches the list addresses $B04F/$B055 and $B052/$B058 into the operands at $B80F and $B801 and writes the frequency entry to the voice's $D400 and $D401, 8 to $D404 and then the control entry to $D404; it counts $B0BB up. When they are equal and $B000 is non-zero it clears $D404-$D406 of the voice. Called by $B176 after the voice loop.
Low byte of the address operand of the LDA ...,X at $B800, overwritten by the drum step with the address of the drum frequency list.
High byte of the address operand of the LDA ...,X at $B800, overwritten by the drum step with the address of the drum frequency list.
Low byte of the address operand of the LDA ...,X at $B80E, overwritten by the drum step with the address of the drum control list.
High byte of the address operand of the LDA ...,X at $B80E, overwritten by the drum step with the address of the drum control list.
Returns in A the OR of the voice flags $F7, $F8 and $F9, which is non-zero while any voice is playing.

Stops all sound: clears the voice flags $F7-$F9, the fade flags $B0BE and $B0C2 and the volume register $D418, sets the keep flags $B0C4-$B0C6 to $FF and writes 8 to the control registers $D404, $D40B and $D412. $B176 jumps to it when a fade-out has run down, and the levels call it when a level is set up (level 2 at $5363, level 5 at $1C5B), when a level ends or the game is over, and in the setup, fire handling and finish of the mask games.
Starts a fade-out: stores A in $B0BE, $B0BF and $B0C0 (so A is also the rate) and clears the fade-in flag $B0C2. No call to it was found in the level 1 snapshot.
Stream command $8A: ends the voice: clears its active flag $F7+X and writes 0 to its control register $D404, then returns.
Stream command $8B: loads the voice's stream pointer $B05B/$B05E from the next two bytes, sets the stream position $B0A8 to 0 and carries on at $B25C.

Low bytes of the handler addresses of stream commands $80-$8D (14 bytes), read by the instruction at $B317 as $B7FE,X with X from $80. With the high bytes at $B88C the handlers are, in order: $B328, $B501, $B51F, $B539, $B552, $B618, $B5AC, $B590, $B5A1, $B5AC, $B85F, $B86A, $B87E, $B552. The entry for $8C is the address of this table, so that command would run data.
High bytes of the handler addresses of stream commands $80-$8D (14 bytes), read as $B80C,X by the instruction at $B31D; the low bytes are at $B87E.

Low bytes of the handler addresses of track commands $F0-$F5 (6 bytes), read as $B7AA,X at $B374 with X from $F0. With the high bytes at $B8A0 the handlers are: $B385, $B38E, $B39D, $B3AE, $B3BD, $B3D2.
High bytes of the handler addresses of track commands $F0-$F5 (6 bytes), read as $B7B0,X at $B37A; the low bytes are at $B89A.
Low bytes of the handler addresses of wave-program commands 0-6 (7 bytes), read as $B8A6,X at $B431. With the high bytes at $B8AD the handlers are: $B442, $B44E, $B462, $B481, $B49A, $B4B7, $B4ED.
High bytes of the handler addresses of wave-program commands 0-6 (7 bytes), read as $B8AD,X at $B437; the low bytes are at $B8A6.
Offsets of the three voices' SID registers from $D400: 00 07 0E (voice 0 at $D400, voice 1 at $D407, voice 2 at $D40E). Read by $B176, $B0EE, $B7B6 and $B7DC.

11 bytes, 00 FF 01 B7 B8 FF 00 00 4C BC B8. The first five are the idle wave program that $B138 gives every voice: command 0 with a wait of $FF frames, then command 1 jumping to its own start at $B8B7. The six after it, FF 00 00 4C BC B8, end in a JMP to $B8BC; the wave driver does not read them, but $B0EE reads some of them as voice offsets ($B8BC for sound row $08, $B8C1 for row $0C), because it indexes $B8B4 with the table position.

Low bytes of the 94-entry table of SID frequency values, with the high bytes at $B920. It is looked up by $B176, $B3F8 and $B711 with a note number plus offsets: the note plus $B08A and $B08D in general, and at $B3F8, which clears $B08A first, the note plus $B08D only. Entry 0 is $0578, entries 1 to 93 rise from $0128 to $EB00.
High bytes of the 94-entry table of SID frequency values (94 bytes); the low bytes are at $B8C2. Entry 0 is $0578 and entry 93 is $EB00.

6 records of 5 bytes, chosen by the offset after stream command $86 or $89 ($B5AC): list address (2 bytes), list length, sustain/release value and pulse width high byte. They are, by offset: 00: list $B99C length $0C sustain/release $E8 pulse high $08; 05: list $B9B4 length $0C sustain/release $D9 pulse high $08; 0A: list $B9CC length $0C sustain/release $D8 pulse high $08; 0F: list $B9CC length $0C sustain/release $B8 pulse high $08; 14: list $B9CC length $0C sustain/release $78 pulse high $08; 19: list $B9CC length $0C sustain/release $38 pulse high $08.

The drum lists the records at $B97E point to, 72 bytes. A list is a run of control register values for $D404 followed by a run of the same length of values that $B7B6 writes to both $D400 and $D401; a record's length is the length of each run. Lists may be shared by several records.

Pulse-width sweep steps, 35 bytes, read by $B64E with the index in $B02C and started by stream command $82; $B32E also reads it, as the pattern address of a track entry. A step is three bytes: a frame count, then the low and high bytes of the amount added to the pulse width each frame. A count of 0 is followed by the index to go back to instead. Programs start at offsets $00, $05, $10 and $1B.

Pitch-slide steps, 84 bytes, read by $B698 with the index in $B035 and started by stream command $83. A step is three bytes: a frame count, then the low and high bytes of the amount added to the voice's frequency each frame. A count of 0 is followed by the index to go back to instead.

7 bytes: the pointer table for stream command $84 (one entry, $BA5D, at $BA5B/$BA5C) and the entry it points to: 01 03 00 05 0C, which gives 1 frame per step, 3 steps and the step values 0, 5 and 12 added to the note. $B698 also reads $BA5B as a slide table, but only when $B032 is non-zero, which nothing sets.

Filter-sweep steps, 26 bytes, read by $B75E with the index in $B048 and started by stream command $85. A step is three bytes: a frame count, then the low and high bytes of the amount added to the filter value. A count of 0 is followed by the index to go back to instead. Programs start at offsets $00, $05, $10 and $15.
10 addresses of wave programs (20 bytes), chosen by stream command $81 with the program number as the index: $BA90, $BA9F, $BAAE, $BAC5, $BAD4, $BB04, $BB13, $BB1F, $BB2F, $BB3B.

The wave programs, 184 bytes, started at the addresses in the table at $BA7C. A program is a list of commands for $B3F8, each a command number 0 to 6 followed by its parameters: 0 waits, 1 jumps to an address, 2 sets attack/decay and sustain/release, 3 sets the control register $D404 and waits, 4 does the same relative to the note end, 5 also changes the pitch, 6 only moves on. The idle program that new voices start with is at $B8B7.

The sound table, 44 bytes: 11 rows of 4 bytes, one per sound effect, so the number passed to $B0EE in X is the row offset. A row has the stream numbers for voices 0 to 2 (an entry with bit 7 set leaves the voice alone) and a zero. Streams by row offset (-- means none): 00: 00 -- --; 04: -- 01 02; 08: 03 -- --; 0C: -- 04 05; 10: -- 06 07; 14: -- 08 09; 18: 0A -- --; 1C: 0B -- --; 20: -- 0C 0D; 24: -- 0E 0F; 28: -- 10 11.

18 addresses of sound streams (36 bytes), indexed by twice the stream number taken from the sound table at $BB48: $BB98, $BB9C, $BBA7, $BBAE, $BBB5, $BBB5, $BBC4, $BBCF, $BBDC, $BBE3, $BBEA, $BBFD, $BC01, $BC06, $BC0D, $BC1F, $BC2E, $BC35. The streams numbered 4 and 5 are the same.

The 18 sound streams, 161 bytes, started from the addresses in the table at $BB74. A stream is a series of entries read by $B25C: a note number below $60 followed by its length in frames, $60 and a length for a rest, or a command $80-$8D with its parameters (for instance $81 and a wave program number, $86 with a drum record offset and a length, $8A to end the voice). Streams 4 and 5 share their data, and streams 8 and 12 run on into the data of streams 9 and 13.
